transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everybody, thanks for joining - I'm Samira with Redwood, AE on this account. We also have Daniel from our SE team. Quick intro, then we'll jump into a live walkthrough of the hosted embeddings + rerank flow.
[00:11] Daniel: Hi all - Daniel Wu, SE. We'll show API calls, Console bits, and our Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.
[00:18] Lena: Thanks, Samira. Quick note, our current infra is Elastic + custom BM25 pipeline, some lightweight transformer rerankers in prod but they're slow. We're hoping for better latency and cost.
[00:29] Samira: Great - curious what your qps and SLOs look like?
[00:33] Lena: Peak ecom traffic is ~120 qps, tail is spiky; target p95 latency for search results is ~200 milliseconds, and cost per query needs to stay in a budget.
[00:44] Imran: Also want to mention we need SOC2 and SSO; data residency for EU customers is a requirement.
[00:50] Samira: Yep, we can cover that - Redwood Hosted API supports regional endpoints and we have SOC2 details in the security pack. We'll share the doc.
[00:57] Daniel: Ok jumping in - here's the basic hosted flow: you send embed requests to /v1/embeddings, we return vectors; these go into your vector store (you can use us or Pinecone/FAISS). For reranking we have a dedicated rerank endpoint that takes top-K candidates and returns relevance scores - you can blend that with BM25.
[01:18] Daniel: (screen-sharing) API example: curl to /v1/embeddings with batch of 128 queries, we recommend batching to amortize overhead; then for rerank we call /v1/rerank with pairs or candidate lists.
[01:32] Imran: How does token cost work for rerank? If we send the whole doc for rerank that could be expensive.
[01:36] Daniel: Good point - reranker is optimized for scoring candidates, not full doc completion. For long docs we recommend sending condensed passages or passage-level chunks. The per-request cost is per-token for the model used by the reranker; we can recommend smaller reranker slabs to reduce spend. Also there's a short-circuit mode where you only request rerank for ambiguous queries (based on confidence thresholds) to save tokens.
[01:55] Lena: And latency - if we do hosted API rerank for each query, will that meet our p95 200ms?
[02:00] Daniel: In most of our hosted deployments we've seen 120-250ms depending on model and region. For strict SLOs we suggest Dedicated or edge routing with smaller model variants. We can also do caching of top-k prefixes to shave time.
[02:13] Priya: Can you explain the caching? We currently cache query results but not KV caches at model level.
[02:18] Daniel: Sure - in the runtime we have prefix/KV caching so for repeated sessions or similar queries the KV cache reduces autoregressive overhead. For rerank we cache embeddings for documents; if your index refresh rate is low, reuse embeddings heavily.
[02:30] Imran: You said model variants - do you have recommended models for dense retrieval + rerank?
[02:34] Daniel: We have curated options: rdx-embed-1 (fast, 256-d), rdx-embed-2 (higher quality, 768-d), and rdx-rerank-1 which is tuned for pairwise scoring. For cost sensitive flows we recommend rdx-embed-1 + lightweight rerank; for high accuracy use rdx-embed-2 + rdx-rerank-1. These are examples - names may vary in the console.
[02:58] Lena: Are those quantized? We run on CPU for some of our infra, can't afford too many GPUs.
[03:03] Daniel: Our embeddings can be exported and quantized for on-prem or used via hosted. For Hosted API we run models in quantization-friendly paths; Dedicated lets you choose quantization levels and kernel selection. The Optimize tool will recommend quantization profiles by workload.
[03:15] Samira: Let me show a quick demo - we'll do a two-step pipeline: 1) embed queries and docs, 2) run a candidate search (your vector DB), 3) call rerank on top-10 candidates and show scoring.
[03:26] Daniel: (typing) I'm going to run an example with a sample product search query - "waterproof hiking jacket" - we're indexing 10k sample docs.
[03:33] [03:33] Daniel: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"inputs":["waterproof hiking jacket"]}' ... (output shown) vector length 768.
[03:44] Daniel: Now hit rerank endpoint: POST /v1/rerank with the top candidates payload - we'll return a score and an explanation token likelii - explanation text is short.
[03:55] Lena: Mm hm - the explanation is helpful for diagnostics.
[03:58] Imran: Any built-in metrics for NDCG or can we push logs to Console?
[04:02] Daniel: Console has per-route dashboards with latency, cost, top queries, and you can upload eval sets to run automated NDCG/Rouge style comparisons via Redwood Optimize. We'll share the eval template.
[04:13] Samira: Quick note on blending - you can combine BM25 score and rerank score; we often slide a weight to keep recall from retrieval and precision from reranker. We have a recommended formula and a small ablation script in the benchmark sheet.
[04:27] [04:27] Lena: Sounds like what we need. Curious about data retention - do you store queries or embeddings? Our legal team is strict.
[04:33] Samira: For Hosted API we have configurable retention; by default logs are retained 30 days but we can enable shorter retention or a private deployment for longer-term control. We also support KMS integration and customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest.
[04:48] Priya: And SSO / SAML?
[04:50] Daniel: Yes - SSO via SAML/Okta is supported; RBAC for team roles in Console, audit logs accessible for compliance. We'll share the SOC2 package and the SSO integration guide.
[05:00] Imran: About pilot - would you recommend Hosted or Dedicated for an initial 1-week pilot?
[05:05] Daniel: Hosted is fastest to get started - you can run a pilot with our hosted endpoints and the eval harness. If you find p95 doesn't meet 200ms, we can switch to Dedicated for the pilot or enable region-specific routing. Many customers start hosted and move to Dedicated later.
[05:20] Samira: For cost modeling, I'll include a couple scenarios: hosted per-token baseline, hosted with batching and thresholded rerank, and Dedicated commit pricing with x GPUs.
[05:29] Lena: We'll need that to present to finance. Also a short write-up for the ML team on how to chunk long docs for rerank.
[05:36] Daniel: I'll add a short note and the sample script for chunking + passage selection.
[05:40] Priya: Any integrations with our existing Elastic cluster? We don't want to rip and replace everything.
[05:45] Daniel: Yes, you can keep Elastic as the primary retriever (BM25) and only call our reranker on top-k. Alternatively, use embeddings for retrieval and keep Elastic as fallback. We support both hybrid flows.
[05:58] Lena: Ok, technical deep dive request: can Daniel and my team schedule a one-hour session next week to run a live benchmark with our logs?
[06:05] Samira: Absolutely - let's tentatively target Nov 21 for the SE-led benchmark session.
[06:10] Imran: We'll prepare sample logs and a 10k doc extract and put it in S3; what's the preferred format?
[06:15] Daniel: CSV of queries with timestamps and a JSONL of documents works well. We'll share the exact template in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:23] Lena: Any gotchas around rate limits during the pilot? We have bursts > 200 qps occasionally.
[06:29] Samira: Hosted has rate limits per account but supports burst/elastic policies. For predictable bursts, Dedicated is better; we can also configure autoscaling/burst capacity. I'll include that in the pricing doc.
[06:41] [06:41] Priya: One legal note - we'll need to vet your subprocessor list.
[06:44] Samira: Understood - I'll have our legal contact send the info and SOC2 pack.
[06:48] Daniel: Quick demo wrap-up - here's the Console screenshot showing per-route latency and cost, the Optimize suggestion panel recommending batch size 64 for your query distribution, and a quantization suggestion for embedding export. (link shown: https://redwood.app/decks/aurorasearch-demo)
[07:05] Lena: That's useful. If we see a +8-12 NDCG improvement in our test set with <= 2x cost, we can justify pilot expansion.
[07:12] Samira: Great - we'll aim for that. Final recap: Samira sends pricing and Dedicated SKU worksheet; Daniel shares benchmark sheet + eval scripts; Imran uploads data; schedule SE deep dive Nov 21; pilot week Nov 29- Dec 6.
[07:28] Priya: Thanks everyone - looking forward to the docs.
[07:31] Samira: Thanks - we'll follow-up in CRM with next-steps and calendar invites.
[07:35] [END]
